title: Tower description of the integral compactly supported direct image
statement:
Work in the standing scheme setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$. On $T_{\mathrm{proét}}$ use the pulled-back integral ring sheaf $R_T=\mathcal O_{E,T}=\varprojlim_n(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_T$, not the discrete constant sheaf $\mathcal O_E$ [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x]. Write $A_{n,T}=(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_T$, $N/\ell^n=N\otimes^L_{R_T}A_{n,T}$, and $\operatorname{red}_TN=(N/\ell^n)_n$ [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, det-sp-reduction-tower-normalized]. The categories $\Dbc$ and $\Dctf$ mean bounded constructible complexes and their finite-Tor subcategories [sk-def-sfb-constructible]; normalized constructible towers have common cohomological and Tor bounds and invertible derived reduction maps [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers].

Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth of pure relative dimension $d$, with a compactification $f=\bar f\circ j$, where $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ is open and $\bar f:\bar X\to Y$ is proper [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and let $M\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$. Use derived module pullback and tensor over these ring sheaves [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], and the separately derived compact-support composite $Rf_{!,\mathcal O_E}=R\bar f_*j_!$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek]. Then:

1. The tower $Rf_{!,\bullet}\operatorname{red}_XM$ is normalized constructible. If $[a,b]$ is a Tor-amplitude interval for $M$, its levels have Tor amplitude in $[a,b+2d]$.
2. There is a canonical isomorphism in $\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$
$$Rf_{!,\mathcal O_E}M\simeq R\varprojlim_nRf_{!,\mathcal O_E/\ell^n}(M/\ell^n).$$
Here the finite levels are restricted to $R_Y$-modules before taking the total derived inverse limit; $Rf_{!,\mathcal O_E}=R\bar f_*j_!$ is independent of the compactification up to canonical natural isomorphism. Consequently
$$(Rf_{!,\mathcal O_E}M)\otimes^L_{R_Y}A_{n,Y}\simeq Rf_{!,\mathcal O_E/\ell^n}(M/\ell^n),\qquad \operatorname{red}_YRf_{!,\mathcal O_E}M\simeq Rf_{!,\bullet}\operatorname{red}_XM.$$
3. For $K\in\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, $f^*_{\mathcal O_E}K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ and its reductions are $f^*_{\mathcal O_E/\ell^n}(K/\ell^n)$. The projection formula
$$Rf_{!,\mathcal O_E}(M\otimes^Lf^*_{\mathcal O_E}K)\simeq Rf_{!,\mathcal O_E}M\otimes^LK$$
holds in $\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$.

proof.text: Put $R_T=\mathcal O_{E,T}$ and $A_{n,T}=R_T/\ell^n$. The ring identifications of [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x] identify the pulled-back condensed integral coefficients, including their scheme-pullback maps, with the completed sheaves used by the ringed-site limit lemmas. The cofinal powers convention in [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers] permits powers of $\ell$ in place of a uniformizer. The standing finite-type $k$-schemes $X$ and $Y$ are Noetherian. Apply [sk-lem-integral-models] to $X$ and the completed ring $R_X$: its equality before clause (1) gives $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)=\Dctf(X,\mathcal O_E)$, and the forward implication of criterion (2), with $K=M$, gives derived $\pi_E$-completeness of $M$. By the cofinal powers convention just cited this is the canonical completion isomorphism for the $\ell^n$ reductions as well. These assertions concern objects over $R_X$, so restriction to the constant coefficient category is not needed. By [det-sp-reduction-tower-normalized], $C_\bullet=\operatorname{red}_XM$ is a normalized constructible derived coefficient tower; its levels have the Tor bounds of $M$. The common cohomological lower bound also puts $C_\bullet$ in $D^+(\operatorname{Tow})$, since tower cohomology is computed levelwise. Thus it is in the domain of the tower direct-image theorem used next. This is an actual derived tower, not only a sequence of isomorphism classes.

source.place: Paragraph (1), first sentence; coefficient conventions made explicit

proof.text:
Let $D_\bullet=Rf_{!,\bullet}C_\bullet$. By [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](1), $D_n=Rf_{!,A_n}C_n$. Our compactification makes $f$ separated of finite type, and smoothness of pure relative dimension $d$ makes every nonempty geometric fibre have dimension $d$. Apply [det-sp-tower-bound-uniform] to $C_\bullet$: its levels are in $\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proét}},A_n)$ with common Tor interval $[a,b]$, the finite rings $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$ are discrete and $\ell$-primary, and the geometric fibre bound is $d$. Its main assertion, applied for each $n$ with $A=A_n$ and $M=C_n$, gives $D_n\in\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},A_n)$, so every level is constructible; its final tower assertion gives the common Tor interval $[a,b+2d]$, together with cohomological vanishing outside that same interval, for all $n$ at once. If $X$ is empty, all levels and direct images are zero and this conclusion is immediate; otherwise the smooth relative dimension is nonnegative, as required by that assertion. For $m\le n$, the reduction map of $D_\bullet$ is
$$D_n\otimes^L_{A_{n,Y}}A_{m,Y}\xrightarrow{b_{n,m}}Rf_{!,A_m}(C_n\otimes^L_{A_{n,X}}A_{m,X})\xrightarrow{Rf_{!,A_m}(\rho_{n,m})}Rf_{!,A_m}C_m=D_m.$$
The first arrow is the canonical comparison $b_{A_n,A_m}$ of the current [det-sp-reduction-direct-image], defined there by the coefficient-extended proper counit and the extension-by-zero tensor comparison. That this composite is the reduction map of the tower $D_\bullet$ is the clause of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] that on simultaneous section models the coefficient projection comparison for the derived direct image, and its composite with open extension, is the derived counit transpose; this is exactly the definition of $b$. Its displayed associativity cocycle for $A_n\to A_m\to A_r$ gives the quotient compatibility used here; the second is invertible because $C_\bullet$ is normalized. This proves normalization, not just a bound on the levels. With the bounds above, it is exactly membership in the normalized constructible category of [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], proving (1).

source.place: Paragraph (1), level calculation, common bounds and the displayed reduction composites

proof.text:
Realize all limits as total right derived inverse limits on strict tower categories. By derived completeness and [sk-def-pe-derived-completion], the completion unit is $M\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n C_n$. The open $j$ is quasi-compact by [lemma-nagata-open-immersion-qc-over-separated-target], applied to $X\to\bar X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: $X$ is finite type over $k$ and $\bar X$ is separated over $k$ in the standing compactification setting. Apply [det-sf-open-closed-extension-zero-limits](2) and then [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] to get the canonical comparison
$$R\bar f_*j_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim_nR\bar f_*j_!\operatorname{Res}_n C_n.$$
In each level, the two factorizations of the ringed-topos morphism $(\bar X,A_{n,\bar X})\to(Y,R_Y)$, through $(\bar X,R_{\bar X})$ or through $(Y,A_{n,Y})$, give
$$R\bar f_*\operatorname{Res}_n\simeq\operatorname{Res}_nR\bar f_{*,A_n}$$
by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. Restriction of scalars is exact because it keeps the underlying sheaf and kernels/cokernels; $j_!\operatorname{Res}_n=\operatorname{Res}_nj_!$ because extension by zero keeps that same scalar action. Apply the same composition comparison on diagram sites to obtain these identifications for the whole tower, with its quotient transitions. The simultaneous section models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] and the level description of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels] identify this tower with $D_\bullet$ after restriction to $R_Y$. Therefore
$$P:=R\bar f_*j_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}L:=R\varprojlim_n D_n.$$
The comparisons preserve the limit projections; no uniqueness of a cone in an ordinary triangulated category is used.

source.place: Paragraph (2), first displayed limit comparison; Stacks 09BP (proetale.tex, lemma-j-shriek-limits), 0A07 and 0D6E (sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim and lemma-derived-pushforward-composition)

proof.text: Apply [sk-lem-sp-tower] to the normalized constructible $D_\bullet$ of Step 2. It gives $L\in\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ and the natural isomorphisms $\epsilon_n:L\otimes^L_{R_Y}A_{n,Y}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_n$. These are the scalar-extension adjoints of the total-limit projections, hence are comparisons with the specified reductions. To record their tower meaning, the underived functor $N\mapsto(N\otimes_{R_Y}A_{n,Y})_n$ is left adjoint to inverse limit: a compatible family of coefficient-linear maps from these tensors to a tower is precisely a map $N\to\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_nD_n$. The tower is a module category on the diagram topos by [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. To identify its left derived functor, choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $Q\to N$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Applying the underived left adjoint gives $(Q\otimes_{R_Y}A_{n,Y})_n$, which computes $\operatorname{red}_YN$ at every evaluation; quasi-isomorphisms between these resolutions remain quasi-isomorphisms after each coefficient extension. For the right derived functor, regard inverse limit and restriction from $A_\bullet$ to the constant ring system $R_Y$ as direct images of ringed diagram topoi. The composition theorem [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] identifies its value with the total derived inverse limit $L=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nD_n$ used in Step 3. Derive the adjunction by [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors], with existence as in [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] and the simultaneous derived section models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Its counit is an actual morphism $\epsilon:\operatorname{red}_YL\to D_\bullet$. Its $n$-th evaluation is $\epsilon_n$, because adjunction evaluates to extension/restriction of scalars at level $n$. For $m\le n$, projecting the limit first to $D_n$ and then along the transition equals projection to $D_m$; taking these adjoints is exactly the quotient compatibility of $\epsilon_n$ and $\epsilon_m$. Thus $\epsilon$ is invertible by joint conservativity in [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](3). Step 3 now gives both the canonical reduction isomorphisms of $P$ and $\operatorname{red}_YP\simeq D_\bullet$, proving (2) for the chosen compactification.

source.place: Paragraph (2), reconstruction and reduction-tower conclusion; Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 3.5.7 (reduction/limit adjunction), Stacks 09T5 (derived.tex, lemma-derived-adjoint-functors)

proof.text: For compactification independence use the existing comparison theorem [det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle] on the input $M$. Its hypotheses hold: $f$ is separated of finite type, $Y$ is qcqs, and $\mathcal O_E$ is an admissible coefficient ring in the explicit list of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. By the integral equality in [sk-lem-integral-models], $M$ lies in $\Dctf(X,\mathcal O_E)$. The definition [sk-def-localizing-closure] contains that entire subcategory, so $M\in\Loc(\Dctf(X,\mathcal O_E))$. This containment uses the definition of the localizing closure in the ambient unbounded module category; it does not impose derived completeness on that closure. The theorem gives natural comparisons $\phi_{c_2,c_1}:R\bar f_{1*}j_{1!}\xrightarrow{\sim}R\bar f_{2*}j_{2!}$ independent of the common refinement, with $\phi_{c,c}=1$ and $\phi_{c_3,c_2}\phi_{c_2,c_1}=\phi_{c_3,c_1}$. By Step 4 both values are in the full subcategory $\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, so these are isomorphisms there as well. This establishes the independence assertion in (2) without inferring equality of derived tower morphisms from equality of their evaluations. Here admissible refers to the coefficient list, not to an ambient exceptional-adjoint or FullCD hypothesis.

source.place: Paragraph (2), compactification independence; existing general compactification-coherence tool

proof.text:
Let $K\in\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$. By [det-lem-int-tensor-pullback], the ordinary inverse image $f^*_{\mathcal O_E}K$ already lies in $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ and needs no further completion. The coefficient identifications of [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x] identify $f^{-1}R_Y$ with $R_X$ and the finite quotient pullbacks with $A_{n,X}$. Apply the derived pullback/tensor isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to $K$ and $A_{n,Y}$ to obtain
$$(f^*K)\otimes^L_{R_X}A_{n,X}\simeq f^*_{A_n}(K\otimes^L_{R_Y}A_{n,Y}).$$
The map is induced on K-flat models by the ordinary tensor pullback comparison. It is natural for $A_{n,Y}\to A_{m,Y}$, so the simultaneous section construction in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] makes these identifications an isomorphism of reduction towers $\operatorname{red}_X(f^*K)\simeq f^*_\bullet\operatorname{red}_YK$. This proves the pullback assertion in (3).

source.place: Paragraph (3), pullback preservation and its reductions; Stacks 07A4 (sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-pullback-tensor-product)

proof.text:
The objects $M\otimes^Lf^*K$ and $P\otimes^LK$ lie in the integral constructible categories by [det-lem-int-tensor-product], since $f^*K$ and $P$ do by Steps 6 and 4. For $U,V\in\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$, use flat-term K-flat representatives $Q,Q'$ from [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]; their reductions remain K-flat by [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings]. The balanced tensor map
$$(Q\otimes_{R_T}A_{n,T})\otimes_{A_{n,T}}(Q'\otimes_{R_T}A_{n,T})\longrightarrow (Q\otimes_{R_T}Q')\otimes_{R_T}A_{n,T},\quad (q\otimes a)\otimes(q'\otimes b)\longmapsto(q\otimes q')\otimes ab$$
has inverse $(q\otimes q')\otimes a\mapsto(q\otimes1)\otimes(q'\otimes a)$. These maps respect the tensor differential, since $a,b$ have degree zero, and commute with every quotient map. The total $Q\otimes Q'$ is K-flat: for an acyclic $V$, first $Q'\otimes V$ is acyclic and then $Q\otimes(Q'\otimes V)$ is acyclic, which equals $(Q\otimes Q')\otimes V$ by reassociation of the total tensor. Its terms are flat since tensoring by a tensor product of flat terms is a composite of exact functors, and sums of flat modules are flat. The derived tensor identifications on these models and their descent are [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Thus
$$\operatorname{red}_T(U\otimes^LV)\simeq\operatorname{red}_TU\otimes^L_{A_{\bullet,T}}\operatorname{red}_TV$$
as derived towers. The computation is the derived coefficient-extension tensor comparison on the simultaneous models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], so it asserts a tower isomorphism rather than an arbitrary lift of level morphisms.

source.place: Paragraph (3), closure under ordinary derived tensor and its reduction formula

proof.text:
Put $C_\bullet=\operatorname{red}_XM$, $B_\bullet=\operatorname{red}_YK$ and $p=\bar f$. The normalized reduction theorem used in Step 1, also applied to $K$, gives bounded-below towers with finite-Tor constructible levels. Construct the canonical map
$$\Phi:(Rp_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}C_\bullet)\otimes^LB_\bullet\longrightarrow Rp_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}(C_\bullet\otimes^Lf^{-1}B_\bullet)$$
as follows. First take the adjoint transpose of the proper counit tensored with $p^{-1}B_\bullet$, using the derived pullback/tensor comparison; then apply $Rp_{*,\bullet}$ to the open-extension projection map, and use $j^{-1}p^{-1}=f^{-1}$. The simultaneous enhanced section models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] supply these derived adjunction, tensor and open-extension comparisons together with all quotient compatibilities. Thus $\Phi$ is an actual morphism of derived towers before any evaluation, not a lift inferred from a family of level arrows. Its $n$-th evaluation is
$$\begin{aligned}
(Rp_{*,A_n}j_!C_n)\otimes^LB_n&\longrightarrow Rp_{*,A_n}(j_!C_n\otimes^Lp^{-1}B_n)\\
&\longrightarrow Rp_{*,A_n}j_!(C_n\otimes^Lf^{-1}B_n).
\end{aligned}$$
For the first arrow use [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-finite](3). Here $B_n$ is in $\Dctf(Y,A_n)$. Also $j_!C_n$ is in $\Dctf(\bar X,A_n)$: apply [det-sp-tower-bound-uniform] to the quasi-compact open $j$, whose geometric fibres have dimension at most zero, with its compactification $(j,\mathrm{id}_{\bar X})$. The given Tor interval for $C_n$ is unchanged by that bound. The schemes are standing schemes and $A_n$ is a finite commutative $\ell$-primary ring. The second arrow is $Rp_*$ of the canonical isomorphism [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula], with inputs $C_n$ and $p^{-1}B_n$. It has no constructibility or field restriction beyond those already satisfied. Hence every evaluation of $\Phi$ is invertible. The unbounded conservativity assertion [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](3) now makes $\Phi$ invertible as a tower map. We use its inverse in the direction
$$Rf_{!,\bullet}(C_\bullet\otimes^Lf^*_\bullet B_\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}(Rf_{!,\bullet}C_\bullet)\otimes^LB_\bullet.$$
Use Steps 6–7 to identify its source input with $\operatorname{red}_X(M\otimes^Lf^*K)$, and Step 4 for $M$ and for $M\otimes^Lf^*K$ to identify both sides with the reductions of $Rf_{!,\mathcal O_E}(M\otimes^Lf^*K)$ and $P\otimes^LK$. Apply the forward implication of [sk-lem-integral-models](2) to each of these already-constructible objects in $D_R(Y)$. Both are derived $\pi_E$-complete; the cofinal powers convention of Step 1 identifies their completion units with the units for the $\ell^n$ towers. Applying total derived inverse limit to the tower isomorphism and using these units [sk-def-pe-derived-completion] yields
$$Rf_{!,\mathcal O_E}(M\otimes^Lf^*_{\mathcal O_E}K)\xrightarrow{\sim}P\otimes^LK.$$
All constructed maps are natural in $M,K$, so this is the asserted natural projection formula in $\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$. It uses no monoidality of inverse limit. The finite-field-only clause (2)(a) of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels] is not applied.

tool_uses.why: Identifies the pulled-back integral ring object with the completed sheaf and supplies its scheme-pullback compatibility; required to apply the generic ringed-site tools to these coefficients.
Supplies derived completeness of integral constructible objects and equality Dbc=Dctf; these are coefficient infrastructure, not an alternate purity route.
Specifies the canonical completion unit used before and after the tower calculation.
The generic quasi-compact-open limit theorem (Stacks 09BP) is needed in the compactification composite.
Supplies the canonical strict-tower derived-pushforward/limit comparison, including its projections, for the proper part of the compactification.
Generic ringed-topos composition identifies the finite-coefficient and restricted completed-coefficient direct images; finite-ring-only comparison nodes would not suffice.
Provides simultaneous varying-ring derived models of tensor, inverse image, direct image and adjunction comparisons so comparisons are morphisms of systems.
Generic derived-adjunction theorem supplies the reduction/total-limit counit of the coefficient-system calculation.
Generic derived functor existence and exact-functor convention needed for the reduction/limit adjunction.
Generic compactification comparison, with independence and cocycle on integral inputs, directly supplies the compactification clause; no purity result is used.
Specifies admissible coefficient rings and contains integral constructible inputs in the domain of the compactification comparison.
Generic integral pullback preservation is needed to ensure the projection-formula input stays constructible.
Generic derived pullback/tensor compatibility proves pullback reduction compatibility without a flat quotient hypothesis.
Generic closure of integral constructible complexes under the uncompleted derived tensor product supplies both projection-formula inputs.
Generic K-flat change of rings justifies computing both finite-coefficient tensors with the displayed reduced representatives.
Generic existence of flat-term K-flat resolutions for the explicit quotient tensor calculation.
Generic site-level descent from the displayed K-flat total tensor isomorphism to a natural derived tensor comparison; a ringed-space-only node would not suffice.
Generic quasi-compactness criterion verifies the open-extension limit theorem hypothesis directly from finite type over k and separated compactification, without an uncited Noetherianity argument.

The finite proper projection map is invertible between standing schemes over the general field; this verifies the levels of the explicitly constructed tower projection map without applying the finite-field-only tower projection theorem.
The finite open-immersion tensor comparison supplies the open part of the compactification projection map over any standing base field.
